name: Supabase, Inc.
origin_detail: Founded 2020 by Paul Copplestone (CEO) and Ant Wilson (CTO); Y Combinator Summer 2020; YC lists Singapore as location; the company is fully remote with staff in 50+ countries
openness_notes: The platform is Apache-2.0 and self-hostable, built by assembling existing MIT/Apache tools around Postgres and open-sourcing whatever it builds itself; revenue comes mainly from the managed hosted platform. That fits level 3 (substantially the whole product OSI-licensed, money from hosting). No relicensing found.

license_history.note: Uses MIT/Apache-licensed tools where they exist; builds and open-sources the rest

risk_events: Growth tied to AI coding tools: >60% of new databases launched through an AI tool (Jun 2026), so demand depends on the 'vibe-coding' boom
Very rapid valuation rise ($5B pre-money Oct 2025 to $10B pre-money Jun 2026) raises expectations
Oct 2026: acquiring Turso (SQLite/libSQL) to serve agent-created databases; integration risk
robustness: Robust open stack: Apache-2.0 and self-hostable on standard Postgres, with 115k GitHub stars, ~10M registered developers and over one million databases launched per week (2026). Well capitalized ($1B raised). Single-vendor stewardship, but users can leave because the core is plain Postgres.
physical_science_relevance: Moderate: used by research groups and lab-automation projects as a quick Postgres backend with auth and realtime APIs for instrument data and dashboards.
openness_effect_assessment: A fully open, self-hostable product on a standard database removed lock-in fears and made Supabase the default backend for AI app builders; it doubled its developer base in eight months and its valuation in eight months (2025-2026) without any licence restriction. Openness appears to have accelerated adoption at no visible cost to monetization of hosting.
key_takeaway: Supabase is the clearest AI-era counterexample to relicensing: a level-3, Apache-2.0 company that grew from founding (2020) to a $10B pre-money valuation (Jun 2026) by being the open, Postgres-based backend that AI coding tools default to. Its risk is concentration on the AI app boom, not openness.
